brief: A shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books, with two drawers.

requirements.requirement: A shelf unit: open shelves for books over more than one storey
requirements.evidence: Three bases on level 0 (piece 0,0,0 full plus half-n bases at -1,0,0 and 1,0,0) with a full base at 0,0,1 on top. Top covers make the shelf surfaces, and a joint bolt locks the bases together. Two storeys are used.

requirements.requirement: Rated to hold 50 kg of books
requirements.evidence: The configurator checks only fit and collisions. It cannot rate load or strength, and those depend on the print material the user picks. Nothing here confirms a 50 kg rating.
drawer:0#-1,0#cut and drawer:0#1,0#cut, one on the cut face of each half base.

A book-row prop sits on the top cover of 0,0,1, and a book stands on the cover of half base -1,0,0. They are staging only. A book could not be placed on the cover of half base 1,0,0: lying flat it was refused because it overlapped the cell wall.

finish.summary: A small two-storey hex shelf unit, 9 parts: three bases on the bottom level with one base above, a joint bolt and covers as shelf surfaces. Two drawers sit in the half bases. Books are staged on it, and check_build found no rule errors and no mesh collisions. The 50 kg load rating is not met: nothing here can check strength.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
